title: Is That So?
text:
The Zen master Hakuin was praised by his neighbors as a man of pure life. A pretty girl whose parents kept a food shop nearby discovered she was pregnant. Her parents were furious and demanded to know who the father was. At first she would not say, but under pressure she named Hakuin.

In great anger the parents went to the master. All he said was, "Is that so?"

When the child was born, they brought it to Hakuin. By then he had lost his reputation, which did not seem to trouble him. He took good care of the baby, getting milk and everything else it needed from his neighbors.

A year later the girl could stand it no longer. She told her parents the truth: the real father was a young man who worked in the fish market. Her mother and father went straight to Hakuin, asked his forgiveness, apologized at length, and asked for the child back.

Hakuin was willing. In handing the child over, all he said was, "Is that so?"
lesson: Do the right thing in front of you even when you are misjudged. A calm heart does not need other people's opinion to stay steady.
people: Hakuin, a village girl and her parents
source: Nyogen Senzaki and Paul Reps, 101 Zen Stories (1919)
caveat: This is a traditional anecdote about the historical Hakuin and is not documented in his own writings.
